intro: Match each development to what it actually established.

right.label: The king cannot tax without the consent of a council representing the realm
The first elected representative assembly in the American colonies
Settlers write their own government and elect their own governor and magistrates
Britain leaves the colonial assemblies alone for over a century, letting self-government take root
Colonists claim a right they say is over 500 years old — not a new demand

rationale.a: Magna Carta, 1215 — English barons forced King John to accept that he could not levy a tax on his own; he needed the consent of a council representing the realm.
rationale.b: House of Burgesses, 1619 — Virginia seated the first elected representative assembly in the colonies.
rationale.c: Fundamental Orders of Connecticut, 1639 — settlers chose their own governor and magistrates by yearly election.
rationale.d: Salutary Neglect — for more than a century Britain's policy left colonial assemblies largely alone, letting self-government take root.
rationale.e: After 1763, colonists argued they were being denied rights of Englishmen held since Magna Carta — a claim about a principle already 500 years old, not a new one.
